We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a portfolio of internally invented, proprietary and wholly-owned oral inhibitors of NOD-like receptor protein 3, or NLRP3. NLRP3 is the upstream driver of sterile inflammation – inflammation that is caused by damage signals, such as cholesterol crystals or misfolded proteins, rather than by infection. NLRP3 activation triggers formation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, an intracellular protein complex involved in the body’s inflammatory response. NLRP3 activation directly stimulates the production of interleukin-1 beta, or IL-1β, and interleukin-18, or IL-18, which are potent pro-inflammatory cytokines. In turn, IL-1β stimulates production of another inflammatory molecule, interleukin-6, or IL-6. For this reason, this inflammatory cascade is referred to as the NLRP3/ IL-1β/IL-6/IL-18 pathway.
When NLRP3 becomes chronically activated, it stimulates this cascade of inflammatory mediators that drive the development and progression of cardiovascular and neuroinflammatory disease. …

sections.title: 15. Risk Factors
text: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. The risks described below are not the only risks that we face. The occurrence of any of the events or developments described below could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects. As a result, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment in our common stock.

Biopharmaceutical drug development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. Since our formation as NodThera Ltd. in 2016, our operations to date have been limited primarily to organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, researching and developing our current pipeline of product candidates, including ruvonoflast and trabzanoflast, building our intellectual property portfolio, undertaking nonclinical studies and IND-enabling activities, conducting and completing Phase 1 clinical trials for ruvonoflast and trabzanoflast, conducting and completing our RESOLVE-1 and RESOLVE-2 Phase 2 clinical trials. We have never generated any revenue from drug sales. We have not obtained regulatory approvals for any of our product candidates.

Typically, it takes many years to develop one new pharmaceutical drug from the time it is discovered to when it is available for treating patients. Consequently, any expectations we have about our future success or viability may not be as accurate as they could be if we had a longer operating history. …

sections.title: Dividend Policy
text: We have never declared or paid cash dividends on our capital stock. We do not intend to pay cash dividends to our stockholders in the foreseeable future. We currently intend to retain all available funds and any future earnings to fund the growth and development of our business. Any future determination to declare dividends will be made at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend on then-existing conditions, including our financial condition, operating results, contractual restrictions, capital requirements, general business conditions and other factors that our board of directors may deem relevant. Investors should not purchase our common stock with the expectation of receiving cash dividends.

In addition, our ability to pay cash dividends on our capital stock in the future may be limited by the terms of any future debt or preferred securities we issue or any credit facilities we enter into.

sections.title: Dilution
text: If you invest in our common stock in this offering, your ownership interest will be immediately diluted to the extent of the difference between the initial public offering price per share of our common stock and the pro forma as adjusted net tangible book value per share of our common stock immediately after this offering. For purposes of this section, shares of our common stock include shares of our non-voting common stock, which have the same economic rights as our common stock.

Our historical net tangible book value as of June 30, 2026 was a deficit of $201.0 million, or $(1,903.12) per share of our common stock. Our historical net tangible book value (deficit) is the amount of our total tangible assets less our total liabilities and the carrying values of our convertible preferred stock, which is not included within stockholders’ deficit. Our historical net tangible book value per share represents historical net tangible book value (deficit) divided by the number of shares of our common stock outstanding as of June 30, 2026.

Our pro forma net tangible book value as of June 30, 2026 was $15.3 million, or $3.69 per share of our common stock. Pro forma net tangible book value represents the amount of our total tangible assets less our total liabilities, assuming the (i) entry into the Term Loan in July 2026 and the borrowing of $15.0 million thereunder, (ii) issuance and sale of an aggregate of 16,389,452 shares of our Series D4 Stock on July 15, 2026, for net proceeds of approximately $15.0 million, (iii) automatic conversion of all outstanding shares of our convertible preferred stock, in the aggregate, into 4,043,751 shares of common stock prior to the completion of this offering, and (iv) filing and effectiveness of our sixth amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will occur immediately prior to the completion of this offering. Pro forma net tangible book value per share represents pro forma net tangible book value divided by the total number of shares outstanding as of June 30, 2026, after giving effect to the pro forma adjustments described above.

sections.title: Business
text: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a portfolio of internally invented, proprietary and wholly owned oral inhibitors of NLRP3. NLRP3 is the upstream driver of sterile inflammation – inflammation that is caused by damage signals, such as cholesterol crystals or misfolded proteins, rather than by infection. NLRP3 activation triggers formation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, an intracellular protein complex involved in the body’s inflammatory response. NLRP3 activation directly stimulates the production of IL-1β and IL-18, which are potent pro-inflammatory cytokines. In turn, IL-1β stimulates production of another inflammatory molecule, IL-6. For this reason, this inflammatory cascade is referred to as the NLRP3/ IL-1β/IL-6/IL-18 pathway.

When NLRP3 becomes chronically activated, it stimulates this cascade of inflammatory mediators that drive the development and progression of cardiovascular and neuroinflammatory disease. This phenomenon of chronically elevated inflammation that persists and contributes to disease progression even when other known risk factors are well controlled, is known as RIR. The presence of RIR can be assessed using a widely available biomarker called hsCRP, which is a well-validated independent risk factor for future cardiovascular events, and hsCRP can also be used to evaluate whether inflammatory activity of the NLRP3/ IL-1β/IL-6/IL-18 pathway has been reduced by a therapeutic intervention. By directly inhibiting NLRP3 upstream, we aim to broadly reduce the activity of the entire sterile inflammation pathway, thereby reducing RIR and modifying the course of cardiovascular and neurologic diseases.

We have been a leader in the research, discovery and development of NLRP3 inhibitors for over a decade, and we have designed our portfolio to address historical challenges faced by other NLRP3 inhibitors: potency, therapeutic index and tissue penetration. …

sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.text:
We measure stock-based awards granted to employees, directors and non-employees based on their fair value on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. Compensation expense for employee and director awards is recognized using the straight-line method over the requisite service period, which is generally the vesting period. We account for forfeitures as they occur. We measure restricted common stock awards using the difference, if any, between the purchase price per share of the award and the fair value of our common stock at the date of grant.

The Black-Scholes model requires inputs including the expected volatility of our common stock, the expected term, the risk-free interest rate and the expected dividend yield. We have historically been a private company and lack company-specific historical and implied volatility information. Therefore, we estimate our expected stock volatility based on the historical volatility of a representative group of public companies in the biotechnology industry. The expected term of our stock options has been determined using the simplified method for awards that qualify as plain-vanilla stock options. The risk-free interest rate is determined by reference

to the U.S. Treasury yield curve. We have estimated a 0% dividend yield.

Research and development expenses increased by $9.5 million to $19.9 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $10.3 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The change was primarily due to an increase in services received under our CRO and CMO arrangements as our clinical trials progressed into later and more cost-intensive stages of activity, mainly reflecting the focus on completing the Phase 2 trial of ruvonoflast. There was a $9.2 million increase in ruvonoflast costs driven by a $7.9 million increase in CRO services fees and passthrough costs to complete Phase 2 trials. Additionally, there was $1.4 million of chemistry, manufacturing, and controls, or CMC work for ruvonoflast as we prepare for Phase 3 trials. The change also reflected a $0.4 million increase in other research and development related costs driven by an increase in research and development employees including the Chief Medical Officer who joined in October 2025. This was offset by a decrease of $0.1 million in safety and toxicology studies that were performed in 2025 with no additional work required in 2026.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses increased by $1.1 million to $4.7 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $3.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The change was primarily attributable to $0.6 million of higher personnel-related costs, largely driven by $0.4 million of stock-based compensation expense and $0.6 million of higher legal, accounting and consulting costs associated with our preparation for becoming a public company. This was offset by a decrease of $0.1 million in travel and entertainment driven by an effort to reduce travel costs.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense), Net
nonop.text: Our other income (expense), net primarily relates to changes in the fair value of our Convertible Notes, for which we elected the fair value option under ASC Topic 825, Financial Instruments, and interest accrued on the Convertible Notes. Changes in fair value attributable to base market risk are recorded in other income (expense), net. Following the conversion of the Convertible Notes into Series D3 convertible preferred stock, or the Series D3 Stock, in April 2025, no further fair value remeasurement was required. Accordingly, the six months ended June 30, 2025 include fair value remeasurement through the conversion date, while the six months ended June 30, 2026 do not include any such remeasurement.
